The Möbius function is defined by μ(1)=1 and, for n>1,
μ(n)={0,(−1)r,​p2∣n for some prime p,n is a product of r distinct primes.​
(1)
It is a multiplicative arithmetic function: μ(mn)=μ(m)μ(n) whenever m and n are coprime.
The summand μ(d)2/ϕ(d) is multiplicative, so its divisor sum is multiplicative. For a prime power pa with a≥1, only d=1,p contribute and
∑d∣pa​ϕ(d)μ(d)2​=1+p−11​=p−1p​=ϕ(pa)pa​.
(2)
Multiplying these local identities over the prime divisors of n gives
d∣n∑​ϕ(d)μ(d)2​=ϕ(n)n​​.
(3)
For the final claim, choose distinct primes p0​,…,pk​. The moduli pj2​ are pairwise coprime, so the Chinese remainder theorem gives an integer a satisfying
a≡−j(modpj2​),0≤j≤k.
(4)
Every positive integer n≡a(mod∏j​pj2​) then has pj2​∣n+j. Hence
μ(n)=μ(n+1)=⋯=μ(n+k)=0​.
(5)
There are infinitely many positive representatives of this congruence class.

3K (Coding and Cryptography)

Words: 162 Articles: 1
Paper 2 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 162
3K OurBigBook.com
For a binary symmetric channel with crossover probability p, the capacity is
C=1−H2​(p),
(13)
where H2​ is the binary entropy. Shannon second coding theorem says that for every transmission rate R<C and every ϵ>0, sufficiently long block codes exist with rate at least R and decoding-error probability below ϵ; conversely, a sequence of codes whose error tends to zero cannot have limiting rate above C.
For the general channel let X and Y be its input and output. Every conditional output distribution is a permutation of (p1​,…,pn​), hence
H(Y∣X)=−∑i=1n​pi​logpi​
(14)
for every input distribution. Since H(Y)≤logn,
I(X;Y)≤logn+∑i​pi​logpi​.
(15)
The uniform input makes every output probability equal to 1/n: the column-permutation assumption and the total sum imply that all column sums are equal to one. It therefore attains H(Y)=logn, proving
C=logn+i∑​pi​logpi​​.
(16)
In the displayed four-output channel each row is a permutation of
(31​,31​,61​,61​).
(17)
With base-two logarithms,
C​=2+32​log31​+31​log61​=2−log3−31​=35​−log3​.​
(18)

For a deterministic finite automaton the extended transition function of a deterministic finite automaton is recursively
δ(q,ϵ)=q,δ(q,wa)=δ(δ(q,w),a).
(19)
The accepted language is
L(D)={w∈Σ∗:δ(q0​,w)∈F}.
(20)
For a nondeterministic finite automaton, δ(q,w) is the set of all states reachable from q while reading w; recursively,
δ(q,ϵ)={q},δ(q,wa)=⋃r∈δ(q,w)​δ(r,a).
(21)
Thus
L(N)={w∈Σ∗:δ(q0​,w)∩F=∅}.
(22)
The powerset construction has state set P(Q), initial state {q0​}, transition
δ(S,a)=⋃q∈S​δ(q,a),
(23)
and accepting states {S⊆Q:S∩F=∅}. Induction on ∣w∣ gives
δ({q0​},w)=δ(q0​,w),
(24)
so the two automata accept exactly the same language. If ∣Q∣=m and F has one state, exactly 2m−1 of the 2m subset states contain it and are accepting, including states that may be unreachable.

A generalized linear model assumes that the independent responses Yi​ have distributions in an exponential family, with means μi​, and that
g(μi​)=ηi​=xiT​β.
(25)
The invertible function g is the link function; it connects the mean to the linear predictor.
For binomial regression, write Yi​∼Bin(mi​,pi​) independently, so μi​=mi​pi​. The logistic regression link is
log1−pi​pi​​=xiT​β,pi​=1+exiT​βexiT​β​,
(26)
while probit regression uses
Φ−1(pi​)=xiT​β,pi​=Φ(xiT​β),
(27)
where Φ is the standard-normal distribution function. The logit is the canonical link function for the binomial family.

Words: 74 Articles: 1
7E OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 74
c OurBigBook.com
Suppose there were no singular point in the Riemann sphere. Then every finite point would be ordinary, so p and q would be entire functions. Ordinary behavior at infinity would force p(z)=2/z+O(z−2) and q(z)=O(z−4). In particular p(z)→0, so Liouville theorem would give p≡0, contradicting the required leading term 2/z. Thus infinity cannot also be ordinary, and every such differential equation has at least one singular point in C.
Solved by gpt-5.6-sol high.

8D OurBigBook.com
Let R be the center of mass and g the uniform gravitational acceleration. The gravitational torque about R is
∑i​(ri​−R)×mi​g=(∑i​mi​(ri​−R))×g=0.
(45)
Choose body-fixed principal axes of inertia. The inertial derivative of the angular momentum is
N=(dtdL​)body​+ω×L.
(46)
For torque-free motion N=0 and Li​=Ii​ωi​, giving the Euler equations for a torque-free rigid body
I1​ω˙1​+(I3​−I2​)ω2​ω3​I2​ω˙2​+(I1​−I3​)ω3​ω1​I3​ω˙3​+(I2​−I1​)ω1​ω2​​=0,=0,=0.​
(47)
For a symmetric top, let I1​=I2​=I and let I3​ be the axial moment. Then ω3​ is constant and
ω˙1​=−Ωω2​,ω˙2​=Ωω1​,Ω=II3​−I​ω3​.
(48)
Thus ω12​+ω22​ is constant and the transverse angular-velocity vector rotates uniformly about the body symmetry axis. Its rate is ∣Ω∣; it precesses in the positive axial sense when (I3​−I)ω3​>0 and in the opposite sense when this product is negative.

ne​=Xe​nb​,nH​=(1−Xe​)nb​.

Xe2​1−Xe​​=ηπ22ζ(3)(2π)3/2​(me​c2kB​T​)3/2eI/(kB​T)​.

Even when kB​T≪I, the high-energy tail of the enormous photon population contains enough ionizing photons per baryon to delay cosmological recombination. 10D (Quantum Information and Computation)

Words: 118 Articles: 1
Paper 2 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 118
10D OurBigBook.com
Apply a Hadamard gate to every qubit. The amplitude of ∣0n⟩ becomes
⟨0n∣H⊗n∣ξ⟩=2n1​∑x∈Bn​​(−1)f(x).
(54)
It equals 1 in case (I) and 0 in case (II). A computational-basis measurement therefore returns 0n with certainty in case (I) and never returns it in case (II). This is the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm.
For the distributed problem, Alice prepares
∣ξA​⟩=2−n/2∑x​(−1)fA​(x)∣x⟩
(55)
using one query to her quantum oracle, and sends these n qubits to Bob. Bob applies his phase oracle, producing
2−n/2∑x​(−1)fA​(x)⊕fB​(x)∣x⟩.
(56)
The function h=fA​⊕fB​ is constant zero in case (1) and balanced in case (2). Bob applies H⊗n and measures as above: outcome 0n identifies case (1), while every other outcome identifies case (2), with certainty.

b OurBigBook.com
For a length-M DFT with M even, split the input into its even and odd entries. Two length-M/2 DFTs determine the result, followed by at most M multiplications by twiddle factors. Hence the multiplication count satisfies
T(M)≤2T(M/2)+M,
(230)
so induction gives T(M)≤CMlog2​M for powers of two. This proves the needed fast Fourier transform bound rather than assuming it.
Part (a) computes the length-2N DFT of the reflected vector y and then recovers
zk​=21​ω2Nk/2​Yk​,0≤k<N.
(231)
Forming y uses no multiplications and the final recovery uses only N. Therefore the discrete cosine transform costs at most
C(2N)log(2N)+N=O(NlogN).
(232)
